summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated Bun-only payload in a UI component package
details: @servicetitan/assist-ui@2.1.2 declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is written in obfuscator.io style (`_0x...` identifiers, per-function string dictionaries hiding literals such as "ldd", "/etc/os-release", "Alpine", "bun", and the Bun release URL) and, on npm install, downloads the Bun runtime archive from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line bundle prefixed with the Bun bytecode-cache marker `// @bun @bun-cjs`, using shuffled string arrays (rotate function plus large mixed constant/opcode array) and hex-mangled identifiers, and is only executable under the Bun runtime — Node cannot load or inspect it. The package advertises itself as a React UI component library ("ServiceTitan Atlas UI Components"), which has no need for a second JavaScript runtime at install time. The combination of preinstall lifecycle execution, obfuscated dropper script, fetch of an alternate runtime, and execution of a Bun-only obfuscated sibling payload with full user privileges matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and evades scanners that only trace Node-resolved code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
